title: Component lifecycle: contribution & deprecation guidelines for tokens, controls, and charts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a clear contribution and deprecation governance document for Redwood's design system that covers tokens, controls (buttons, tables), and data visualizations (charts). This ticket consolidates: contribution steps, an approver checklist, RFC workflow, and a predictable deprecation policy so product teams can plan migrations and engineers can estimate effort. The result should be a single authoritative page in Confluence + a lightweight RFC template in GitHub (design-rfcs) and a checklist that maintainers run during PR review.
background: We have had ad-hoc PRs adding tokens and components which later required breaking changes or cross-platform fixes. Recent incidents: ENG-2198 (token export regressions) and a customer bug where a table change caused visual diffs in multiple apps. Teams need an explicit low-friction governance flow that preserves velocity but avoids regressions and churn.
acceptance_criteria: A Confluence page exists titled 'Design System: Contribution & Deprecation Guidelines' with sections for tokens, controls, and charts
A 5-item reviewer checklist is embedded in the repo CONTRIBUTING.md and surfaced by the PR template
An RFC template is published in github.com/redwood/design-rfcs and linked from Confluence
Deprecation flow is defined with timelines, codemod requirements, and telemetry requirements for token and component removal
At least one example migration (button token rename) is captured and has a codemod PR linked from the doc
tasks: Create GitHub RFC template and initial RFC draft (owner: Asha)
Add review checklist to design repo CONTRIBUTING.md (owner: Design Ops)
Coordinate with ENG to define codemod policy and telemetry events (dependency: ENG-2198)
Publish and announce to internal #design-system and #eng-changes channels
review_checklist: Design intent documented: purpose, visual spec, states
Accessibility: keyboard behavior, focus styles, color contrast for tokens
Cross-platform mapping: React props vs mobile tokens/Android/iOS equivalents
Visual regression tests added to Storybook/regression suite
Performance: charts must include data-sampling/virtualization guidance if >1000 points
Backward compatibility: migration strategy for breaking changes and token renames
Docs: usage examples, theming notes, migration docs included in PR
Owner and rollback plan specified: who to contact and how to revert
rfc_process: When change affects public API (props, tokens, theme keys) file an RFC in github.com/redwood/design-rfcs using the template
RFC fields: summary, motivation, alternatives considered, migration plan, telemetry/events needed, estimated effort
RFC review window: 7 business days for comments, maintainers mark 'accepted' or 'needs revision'
If RFC affects infra or runtime cost (e.g., changes to batching/serialization for chart data), include ENG and Infra reviewers explicitly
Once accepted, link RFC from the Confluence page and create a tracking Linear ticket per implementation (ENG- / PM- as needed)
deprecation_flow: Phase 0 — Proposal: Add deprecation note to Confluence and open a 'deprecation RFC' if cross-team impact. Notify channels: #design-system, #product-notices.
Phase 1 — Announce (Day 0): Public deprecation announcement with rationale, replacement guidance, and migration docs. Add a 'deprecated' flag in token JSON and component Storybook examples.
Phase 2 — Alias period (Day 0–90): Keep legacy token/component working but alias to the new token. Ship codemod and migration guide. Track usage via telemetry and list top consumers.
Phase 3 — Soft removal (Day 90–180): Remove direct exports but keep runtime fallback for 180 days; raise warnings in dev console. Start blocking new use in new PRs.
Phase 4 — Hard removal (Day 180+): Remove implementation and exports. Update CHANGELOG and close deprecation RFC. Provide post-mortem if customer impact occurred.

Additional rules: For tokens used in external customer contracts, escalate to Product and Legal; deprecation timelines may extend. Any removal that alters visible UX requires accessibility re-test and QA sign-off. Create codemods for any token rename with >10 repo references.
migration_examples: Button token rename: primary-bg -> btn-primary-bg. Codemod PR: github.com/redwood/design/codemods/pulls/12
Table row-height token consolidation: table-row-compact -> table-row-density. Migration guide: confluence.redwood.internal/display/DS/Table+Row+Density
Chart color tokens: moved from chart.color.* to tokens.dataViz.color.* and published alias map in tokens.json

notes: Trade-offs considered: strict central gating slows small fixes vs. light governance that relies on post-merge fixes. We choose a lightweight gate (PR checklist + RFC for API changes) to preserve velocity.
Decision owner: Design Ops for tokens and component semantics; Component maintainers are final approvers for implementation details.
Follow-up: Add automatic PR bot that reminds authors to link RFC and checklist items when files in 'packages/design-tokens' or 'packages/components' are modified.
